capabilities.target: Researcher sub-agent investigating a stuck account row
CRM account rows (industry, size, headquarters fields)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of 40,000 CRM account rows; ~3% have malformed company names that never return a complete enrichment result

instructions.note: Instruction says to retry or spawn a researcher sub-agent and 'keep going until every row is complete,' with no termination condition, retry cap, or spawn-depth limit. Combined with ~3% of rows (about 1,200 per night) that can never complete, this guarantees indefinite retries and recursive sub-agent spawning every run.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota, shared with sales and marketing teams
Spawned researcher sub-agent (can itself spawn further researchers)
Sales and marketing tools dependent on the shared enrichment quota

controls.name: Maximum unattended steps and runtime limit for the enrichment run
controls.decay_rationale: A hard step/runtime ceiling enforced by the orchestrator does not depend on model behavior and does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Per-run and per-day spend cap or call-rate limit on enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: A spend cap enforced at the billing/API gateway layer holds regardless of model reasoning, though it only narrows (not severs) the path; low-and-slow spend could still accumulate under the cap over many nights.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and count limit
controls.decay_rationale: A depth/count limit enforced by the spawning framework does not depend on the model choosing to stop.

controls.name: Dedicated enrichment-agent API credential/quota, isolated from sales and marketing tools
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the credential so the agent cannot draw down a quota shared by other teams removes the cross-team blast radius regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Spend/usage anomaly alert on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; reduces time-to-detection but does not prevent spend or quota exhaustion.

controls.name: Per-row retry cap with fail-closed escalation to manual review instead of recursive spawning
controls.decay_rationale: A hard per-row retry ceiling enforced outside the model's own judgment of 'looks incomplete' prevents indefinite retries on rows that can never complete.

findings.title: Toxic combination (TC6 Spend loop, compounded by recursive delegation): unbounded retry + sub-agent spawning on permanently-malformed rows exhausts a cross-team shared quota

attack_path.note: ~1,200 of 40,000 nightly rows (3%) have malformed company names that never return a complete lookup result
Prompt instructs the agent to retry failed/incomplete lookups with no retry cap; each retry is billed per call
Prompt instructs spawning a researcher sub-agent when a lookup 'looks incomplete,' with no spawn count or depth limit
Researcher sub-agents can spawn further researchers, each of which can again call cap.enrich_lookup, with no bound on recursion
All calls draw on one API key and monthly quota shared with sales and marketing
Once the shared quota is exhausted, sales and marketing tools stop working until the next month

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. Sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call. The API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.
The nightly batch is 40,000 rows. Roughly 3 percent of rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.
If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account. Keep going until every row is complete.

recommendations.action: Add a hard maximum on unattended steps/runtime for the nightly run and a maximum spawn depth and total sub-agent count for cap.spawn_researcher.
Enforce a per-row retry cap (e.g. 2-3 attempts); on exceeding it, fail closed by flagging the row for manual review instead of escalating to a sub-agent.
Give the enrichment agent its own API credential and quota, isolated from the sales and marketing teams' shared key, so runaway enrichment cost cannot take down other teams' tools.
Add a per-run and per-day spend cap on enrich.lookup enforced at the API gateway or billing layer, independent of the agent's own behavior.
Add spend and call-volume anomaly alerting on the enrichment account so unexpected consumption is caught before the monthly quota is exhausted.

rating.rationale: Source in.crm_rows is internal (I) and the reachable sinks (cap.enrich_lookup = spend, cap.spawn_researcher = delegate) are both S3 severe, giving an inherent tier of high per the base matrix; the autonomy modifier applies (A4_fully_autonomous, can_spawn_agents true, max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes both null) and pushes inherent to the critical cap. No declared or verified controls cover this path: there is no step/runtime limit, no per-row retry cap, no spend cap, no recursion limit, no quota isolation, and no spend alert, so no rubric credit applies at any step and residual equals the inherent floor, critical. This is a present-day, near-deterministic outcome, not a future scenario: 3 percent of every 40,000-row nightly batch (about 1,200 rows) is guaranteed to be permanently malformed, and the prompt's only instruction for that case is unbounded retry or recursive sub-agent spawning against a quota shared with sales and marketing, so the forecast tier equals the residual tier at critical with no additional trigger required. Likelihood is rated almost_certain rather than the rubric guide's default of 'possible' for an internal source, because the trigger condition (malformed rows) is a deterministic property of every nightly batch rather than an adversarial event; this judgment is recorded here per rubric section 8.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP configuration, IaC, or orchestration runtime config was provided; the absence of step, retry, spend, and recursion limits is inferred from the prose runtime notes rather than from a config file, so exact enforcement points are not independently verified (confidence on mechanism detail is medium even though confidence on the finding itself is high given the explicit statements in the notes).

No information was provided on validation logic for cap.crm_write (for example, whether partial or low-confidence enrichment results can be written); the prompt implies writes occur only once a row is judged complete, so this was not scored as a separate finding, but it was not independently verified either.
